title: Project: a local AI service with a database
summary: Connect a tiny text classifier to a validated HTTP endpoint and SQLite.

sections.title: Connect the pieces
paragraphs: An AI application is more than a model. It receives input, validates a contract, performs inference, stores a useful record, and returns a clear result. This project fits a tiny nearest-example text classifier, exposes POST /predict, and records the predicted category in SQLite.

The four training phrases are original fixtures. The classifier uses token-set overlap and returns review when no word matches. It is intentionally modest so the service and data flow stay visible. Replace it with an evaluated model only after the surrounding contract works.

sections.title: Run locally, then extend deliberately
paragraphs: Save the downloaded file and run python project-local-ai-api-and-database.py. The default mode performs a self-test without opening a server. Add --serve to bind to 127.0.0.1:8000; stop with Ctrl+C. In another terminal, POST JSON such as {"text":"reset password"} to /predict. Results are saved in academy_predictions.sqlite3 in the current folder.

The service restricts request size, checks content type and schema, avoids storing raw text, and uses parameterized SQL. It is a local learning service, not a public deployment template: public use also needs a production server, HTTPS, authentication, authorization, rate limits, and operational monitoring.

code.explanation: The database stores only a category and ID. The default self-test avoids starting a long-running process; --serve explicitly enables the local server.

steps: Start the server with --serve and POST a valid JSON request to /predict using your HTTP client.
Send an empty text field and confirm a 400 response; send text/plain and confirm 415.
Inspect the SQLite predictions table and verify invalid requests did not insert rows.
practice.solution: A valid request returns an ID and label, such as account. Invalid input returns a structured error before the INSERT. To extend it, add model_version and created_at fields, then test migrations and authorization before any public deployment.
practice.expected: The default mode prints Self-test passed. In server mode, a valid prediction creates one SQLite row.

quiz.question: Why use placeholders in the INSERT statement?
options: They keep values separate from SQL syntax
quiz.explanation: Parameterized SQL treats the category as data rather than executable SQL. Access control and encryption are separate concerns.
